dish.title: Gyudon: Japanese Simmered Beef and Onion Rice Bowl
dish.description: A 25-minute Japanese comfort bowl: thinly sliced beef and sweet onion simmered in a gingery soy, mirin, and sugar broth until tender, ladled with its juices over steamed short-grain rice and topped with scallions and pickled red ginger.

recipe_version.title: Gyudon: Japanese Simmered Beef and Onion Rice Bowl
recipe_version.description: A 25-minute Japanese comfort bowl: thinly sliced beef and sweet onion simmered in a gingery soy, mirin, and sugar broth until tender, ladled with its juices over steamed short-grain rice and topped with scallions and pickled red ginger.

ingredients.name: short-grain white rice
ingredients.preparation: rinsed until the rinse runs clear

steps.title: Start the rice and prep
steps.body: Combine the rinsed rice and 2 1/3 cups water in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low 15 minutes, then rest covered; it cooks inside this prep and the simmering (overlap stated). Slice the onion and scallions and grate the ginger.

steps.title: Simmer the onion
steps.body: In a 10-inch skillet combine 1 cup water, the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and ginger and bring to a simmer over medium. Add the onion and simmer until soft, 6 minutes.

steps.title: Add the beef
steps.body: Add the beef, separating the slices with chopsticks, and simmer gently, skimming any foam, until just cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes.

steps.title: Rest the rice and serve
steps.body: Take the rice off the heat and let it rest covered 4 minutes, then fluff it and divide among deep bowls. Ladle the beef, onion, and some broth over the rice and top with scallions and pickled ginger.
